Akash THESIS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/h2\u003E\u003Cp\u003EETIOLOGY, INCIDENCE AND OUTCOME OF POTASSIUM ABNORMALITIES IN ICU PATIENTS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClaude Bernard wrote that ‘the constancy of the internal milieu is the \nessential condition to a free and independent life’. Potassium is the most \nabundant cation in the human body, with total body stores amounting to 50 \nmmol\/kg in adults. Less than 2% of K+\n is located extracellularly, and kalemia is \nmaintained in the narrow range of 3.5–5.0 mmol\/L.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg alt=\"\" data-original-height=\"712\" data-original-width=\"831\" height=\"300\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEgQavxQB07GV8Riqf7ChEg51cTuLoHvhXeGV3V64cDa5kNxfwmGybgjPY5mxtXapYHUb7SQbWxu7hvLPIoccEBkMrdsSSR7cVd2jF213n5dNPkKQhJcOsqvPWFOaIZ69OQLhNQRsWK2vs4AdNYT7-NEBuZo4PsPHCiKeuWciR3jwA7TH0yewYLe2Z44gPo=w449-h300\" width=\"449\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPotassium (K+) is an important electrolyte that has been proven essential for normal functioning of the cardiovascular system, skeletal muscle, internal organs, and nervous system. The intracellular proportion of K+, which represents more than 98% of the total body K+, controls cell metabolism and the resting membrane potential. Intracellular K+ is essential for excitability and automaticity of myocardial cells and for the normal functioning of other cells. The normal serum K+ level is 3.5 to 4.5 mEq\/L.\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: x-small;\"\u003E¹ ²\u003C\/span\u003EAn abnormal K+ level predisposes a patient to serious complications, especially cardiac arrhythmia and muscle weakness, which may provoke sudden cardiac arrest and\/or respiratory failure. Critically ill patients are at risk for alterations in their serum K+ level. Reduced kidney function, the presence of metabolic acidosis, use of mechanical ventilation, and increases in cell turnover promote K+ accumulation. Certain medications such as insulin, sympathomimetic agents, and diuretics decrease serum K+, while spironolactone, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, and angiotensin receptor antagonists increase serum K+. Hypokalemia and hyperkalemia can both induce cardiac arrhythmias .³ ⁴\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAIM\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETO FIND OUT ETIOLOGY, INCIDENCE AND OUTCOME OF POTASSIUM ABNORMALITIES IN ICU PATIENTS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOBJECTIVES\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) To identify the spectrum of potassium abnormalities in ICU patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)To study the clinical and laboratory profile of the spectrum of\u0026nbsp; potassium abnormalities in ICU patients\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)To assess the various factors influencing the causation and recovery potassium abnormalities in those patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY DESIGN :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProspective study design with analysis of factors influencing the outcome of the patients with hypokalemia and hyperkalemia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINCLUSION CRITERIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) Patients above the age of 18 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) Patients with \u0026lt;3.5 and \u0026gt;5 of K+ in ICU.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Patients who are willing for study and giving consent for the purpose of study.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEXCLUSION CRITERIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) Patients under the age of 18 years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) Patients\/Patients attendants who are not willing for study or not giving consent for the purpose of study\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Patients without any factors or conditions associated potassium imbalance.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPLACE OF STUDY: Department of General Medicine, Kamineni Institute of Medical Sciences, Narketpally.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY PERIOD:\u0026nbsp;
